title: Nothing to Hide? Then Why Draw the Curtain?
summary: An episode arguing that privacy is not a privilege only the guilty care about but the minimum room in which a person can be themselves; it compares Bentham's panopticon and Foucault's claim that the mere possibility of being seen alters behavior with Arendt's public-private distinction, Rachels's and Nissenbaum's accounts of information flow, and the prohibition of tecessüs alongside the virtue of setr (covering) in Islamic ethics. Through location permissions, read receipts, family-tracking apps and consent texts, it examines how the watched human being changes.
